questions.question: What is the safest invariant for data stored in Memcached?
options: Every cached value is automatically replicated to another node
The application can reconstruct or refetch the value after a miss or eviction
A zero TTL makes the value durable
The cache is the authoritative transaction log
questions.explanation: Memcached is a disposable acceleration layer. The durable source and application miss path must be able to reconstruct every cached value.

questions.question: Traffic is 100,000 requests per second at a measured 94% hit rate. How much traffic reaches the source because of misses?
questions.explanation: The miss rate is 6%, so 100,000 x 0.06 = 6,000 requests per second reach the source before retries or refill duplication.

questions.question: Why does naive hash(key) modulo server-count routing make a pool resize risky?
options: It encrypts keys with the old server count
It changes the destination for most keys and can create a large miss wave
It prevents clients from setting TTLs
It forces every value into one slab class
questions.explanation: Changing the modulus changes most key-to-node assignments. Consistent hashing limits remapping to a much smaller share, reducing refill pressure.

questions.question: A very hot key expires while 500 requests arrive together. Which control most directly prevents 500 simultaneous source reads?
options: Single-flight refill or a meta-protocol recache lease
questions.explanation: Refill ownership lets one caller rebuild the key while peers wait or use a fallback, containing the stampede at the miss boundary.

questions.question: Two refill requests read source versions 7 and 8, but version 7 finishes last. What protects the cache from ending with version 7?
options: CAS/version checks or immutable versioned keys
questions.explanation: A guarded write rejects an update based on an obsolete observed version. Versioned keys avoid overwriting the newer object at all.

questions.question: What does an eviction counter tell an operator?
options: The database permanently lost a row
A non-expired item was removed to make room in its memory class
questions.explanation: Evictions indicate memory pressure within slab/LRU behavior. Correlate them with hit rate, item sizes, source load, and class statistics.

questions.question: Which protocol should a new Memcached client prefer when it needs anti-stampede and stale-serving features?
questions.explanation: Current Memcached documentation recommends the meta protocol for new clients; it supports recache ownership, stale handling, efficient metadata access, and extensible flags.

questions.question: Which production deployment is acceptable?
options: A private, least-privilege cache path with TLS where required and a tested source fallback
A cache used as the only copy of account balances
A pool whose node-loss behavior has never been load-tested
questions.explanation: Memcached belongs on a restricted network path. Protect data in transit where required, minimize sensitive values, and prove that misses and node loss cannot overwhelm the source.
